name: as-any
description: `as any` erases the type checker at that expression — on money and multi-tenant paths that's where a mispriced charge or a cross-org data leak hides. `(req as any)` and `(req.user as any).id`-style casts have typed replacements (AuthenticatedRequest + req.user.id, getOrganizationId(req)); Express-internals monkey-patches are the residual baseline. This ratchet freezes the count and drives it strictly DOWN — lower baselineCount whenever a reduction lands.
lastBumpNote: 1360 -> 1358 on 2026-08-18: FOUNDER KILL RULING — the campaign-ROI endpoint. Both casts lived in the deleted `calculateCampaignROI`: `(campaign as any).totalCost` and `(campaign as any).totalSent`. Worth naming what they were hiding, because it is the reason the function was killed rather than fixed — the cast let a `campaigns` row be read for fields the schema may not declare, and the value that came back fed `cost`, which fed a `revenue = leadCount * 500` invention returned to the caller as ROI. A cast that erases what a row actually contains, sitting directly upstream of a fabricated business metric. Not a typing improvement: a deletion, which remains the cheapest way to satisfy any of these gates. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1364 -> 1360 on 2026-08-17: the four `as any` casts on `agent_memory` inserts, and each one was LOAD-BEARING FOR A DEFECT rather than incidental. `agent_memory` has organization_id (NOT NULL, FK), key (NOT NULL) and value (jsonb, NOT NULL), and NO `content` column at all. Three writers (agentKnowledgeGraph.shareKnowledge, companyAgents.storeMemory, overrideLearner) wrote a `content` field that does not exist while omitting organization_id and value — companyAgents omitted key as well. Every one of those inserts violated NOT NULL, threw, and was swallowed by an empty `catch {}`; agentKnowledgeGraph's catch comment even blamed a "duplicate key", and the table has no unique constraint that could raise one. So knowledge sharing, company-agent memory and override learning had each NEVER PERSISTED A SINGLE ROW while their return values and logs implied success — a system reporting work it never did, which is the fabrication failure mode in its quietest form. The cast is precisely what let a nonexistent column and three missing NOT NULLs type-check. The fourth (ai/executive.ts) supplied every column correctly and its cast was vestigial; removing it changed nothing, which is how you can tell the other three were different. Found by the §55 raw-corpus reconciliation against the corpus invariant "AcreOS's knowledge graph must never become a path around tenancy", and these functions sit in exactly the blind spot `check-org-scoped-fetch.mjs --blind-spot` measures, which is why no tenancy gate had ever objected. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1391 -> 1390 on 2026-08-14: complianceGate's strict-mode fail-open. The removed cast was `const user = req.user as any` in the audit-log write, replaced by `req.user as { id?: string }` — which is what the entry actually needs. The erasure was load-bearing in a small way: the old line read `userId: user?.id || user?.id`, the same expression twice, and `any` is why nothing objected to a fallback that could not differ from what it fell back from. That write is the EVIDENCE half of strict mode, so a silently wrong userId on it is a compliance record naming nobody. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. Five `(orgRecord as any)?.settings?.va_tasks` / `va_scheduled_tasks` reads are gone, and the cast is exactly what let those fields stay undeclared: an undeclared field in `organizations.settings` cannot be carried by a typed write and can be ERASED by one (unit 43). PRIOR NOTE — 1397 -> 1396 on 2026-08-13: document-intelligence tenant scoping. `GET /documents/:id/text` opened with `const doc = await documentIntelligenceService.uploadDocument as any; // placeholder to get fileUrl` — a method REFERENCE cast to any, assigned, and never used, sitting above a handler that then took the fileUrl from `req.query` instead. The cast is what let a placeholder line look like code: `uploadDocument as any` type-checks, so nothing ever asked why a route was holding an unbound method. PRIOR NOTE — 1405 -> 1404 on 2026-08-12: the per-org simulation kill-switch, declared. server/storage/orgRepo.ts read `(org as any)?.settings?.simulationMode` because `organizations.settings.$type<>` did not declare the field — so the flag that stops all real-world sends for an org sat OUTSIDE the contract its own column publishes: no typed write could carry it, and a typed write that replaced rather than merged would have erased it silently. Declaring `simulationMode?: boolean` removed the cast and let the read type-check. The cast was not incidental here — it was the thing that let the omission persist. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 1406 -> 1405 on 2026-08-12: integration-credential shape consolidation. POST /api/integrations/:provider/test read `(integration.credentials as any).encrypted` — guarded only by "are there credentials at all", so a key stored in the OTHER shape (the plaintext one the BYOK panel in Settings wrote) reached JSON.parse as `undefined` and the route threw a 500 instead of answering. The cast was load-bearing for the bug: it erased the fact that `credentials` has no guaranteed `encrypted` field. Replaced by readIntegrationCredentials(), which is typed against the caller's expected bag and returns null rather than erasing. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. minimaNote: VACUITY FLOOR on the SCAN POPULATION, not a ratchet. baselineCount above counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a scan that stops seeing files finds zero and reports it as progress: a zero baseline PASSes on an empty file set, and a nonzero one prints a stale-high "lock it in" for a number that was never true. MEASURED 2026-08-16: this config matched 1370 file(s) (server/**/*.ts minus tests). Floor set to 1100, comfortably below that, so a broken glob or walk trips it while ordinary deletion does not. Checked BEFORE the baseline comparison by scripts/ratchet.mjs; a MISSING floor fails as loudly as a breached one. If a real deletion wave shrinks this population, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave here — never raise it to silence something, never delete the key. Re-measure with `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --measure`.
